description.message: Your own list of which email address or username you gave to which website. Kept on this device only.

ar_lead.message: Which email address or username you gave to which website. If spam arrives on one address, you know who passed it on.

ar_disp_summary.message: Make a disposable address (free, no sign-up)

ar_disp_intro.message: Klin asks the free service **mail.tm** for a new random address. Write the site in the form above first, then press the button. You read what arrives right here.

ar_disp1.message: Good for sign-ups, trials and anything you can afford to lose.

ar_disp2.message: **mail.tm can read every message sent to it** and may delete the address at any time. Never use it for your bank, your main accounts or password recovery.

ar_disp3.message: Pressing the button contacts api.mail.tm with your IP address. Klin asks your permission first.

ar_plus_summary.message: Make a plus address from my own email

ar_plus_note.message: Gives **me+site@example.org**. It works only with some providers, and it still shows your real address: anyone can strip the “+site” part. A real alias from a service you choose is better: paste it above. Klin runs no alias service.

ar_not1.message: **It does not create permanent aliases.** It remembers the ones you made with a service you choose. Disposable addresses come from mail.tm.

ar_not2.message: ==It is kept on this device only==, in your Klin profile, not encrypted. Anyone who can open your profile can read it. Nothing is sent anywhere, and there is no sync.

ar_not3.message: **It cannot prove who leaked an address.** It tells you who you gave it to. A site can also be breached.

ar_not4.message: The password of a disposable address stays in this browser only and is not in a backup file: after loading a backup its inbox cannot be opened.

ar_not5.message: A backup is a plain file. Keep it where you keep your private files.

ar_err_email.message: That does not look like an email address.

ar_err_site.message: Write the site it was given to.

ar_err_backup.message: That file is not a Klin alias backup.

ar_plus_err.message: Write your address above, and the site in the form.

ar_who_none.message: That address is not in your list.

ar_backup_saved.message: Backup saved as klin-aliases.json. It is a plain file.

ar_backup_loaded.message: Added {1}, skipped {2} (already there or not valid).

ar_d_needsite.message: Write the site this address is for, in the form above, first.

ar_d_noperm.message: Without your permission to contact the service nothing was sent.

ar_d_created.message: Created {1} and saved it in your list.

g_lead.message: In a few steps: stop giving every website your real address. Klin shows you the way. Klin runs nothing for this.

g_s1_p1.message: Today you give your real email address to every site. They sell it, leak it, or use it to recognise you everywhere.

g_s1_p2.message: A **mail gateway** gives you a different address for each site. Everything arrives in your normal mailbox, but ==the site never learns who you are==.

g_s1_p3.message: If one address gets spam, you know who passed it on, and you close only that one. If a site is breached, your real address is not in it.

g_s1_p4.message: Klin does not run a gateway and never will. You use one that you choose, or one on your own domain. Klin only explains it and keeps your list.

g_s2_q.message: Do you own an internet domain (like yourname.org)?

g_s2_no.message: No, I want the easy way: a service that does it for me

g_s2_yes.message: Yes, I want to use my own domain

g_s2_no_d.message: You make an account with a service. It forwards mail to you. It can see the mail that passes through it.

g_s2_yes_d.message: No third party between the site and you, except your own mail provider. It takes a little more work.

g_a3_p1.message: These two publish their code, so anyone can check it. Plans, limits and prices change: read them on their site before you decide.

g_a3_p2.message: Klin does not recommend one. Being named here is not an approval. You make the account on their site, not in Klin, and they see your address and the mail that passes through them.

g_a4_p1.message: On the service's site, make one new address for one website you use. Give it a name you will recognise, like the site's name.

g_a4_p2.message: Then use that address on that website, instead of your real one. You can change it in the website's account settings.

g_d3_p1.message: A domain you own, and a mail provider that lets you ==receive everything sent to that domain== in one mailbox. This is often called “catch-all”.

g_d3_p2.message: Not every provider offers it, and some charge for it. Check your provider's help pages. Klin cannot see your account and cannot change it.

g_d4_p1.message: In your provider's settings, turn on catch-all for your domain, so that mail to any name before the @ reaches your mailbox.

g_d4_p2.message: Test it: send a message from another address to a name you invented. If it arrives, it works.

g_d4_p3.message: Your provider can see your mail, like always. Anyone who guesses a name on your domain can write to you: if one address gets spam, close it by changing that name in your mail settings.

g_d5_h.message: Make an address for a site

g_d5_result.message: Use this address on that website:

g_d5_err.message: Write your domain and the website.

g_save_p.message: So that later you know who got which address, and who passed it on.

g_saved.message: Saved. You can see it in your list.

g_not1.message: **It does not make you anonymous.** Sites still see your internet address. This hides only your email address.

g_not2.message: **The service or provider can read the mail that passes through it.** Choose one you trust, and do not use these addresses for your bank.

g_not3.message: Klin runs no gateway, makes no account for you and sees nothing of your mail. This guide loads nothing from the internet.
